# Native Muscle Excitation Replay

## Status and Scope

Provisional development evidence for F07/F08 (#11791/#11792), not a qualified
full-swing result. `tour_matching.muscle_replay` runs a fresh native OpenSim
model from every named continuous initial state. The early implementation
supports muscle forces and gravity only. Non-muscle actuators, other forces
(including contact forces pending their explicit policy), pre-existing
controllers, prescribed motion/coordinates, locks and unsupported constraints
are rejected through recursive component auditing, including components outside
legacy ForceSet/ControllerSet containers. Recursively owned muscle paths must
match the native muscle registry, preventing an undeclared undriven muscle. The early muscle-law domain policy
supports Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle and Thelen2003Muscle with active activation
and compliant tendon dynamics. Ignored activation/tendon modes fail before
native initialization; other laws require explicit domain qualification.
Initial and sampled trajectory activation/fiber state must respect each native
instance's minima without clipping, and fiber length must remain positive.
The zero-pennation Thelen fixture has a zero native minimum fiber length;
the Millard numerical floor must not be copied to it. Contact geometry counts
are metadata, not evidence of contact dynamics. Full anatomical/contact model
qualification and capture matching remain open.

## Equations and Input Boundary

For excitation samples $e_{i,k}$ at physical times $t_k$ in seconds, the native
time-only input player uses

$$e_i(t)=(1-\alpha)e_{i,k}+\alpha e_{i,k+1},\qquad
\alpha=(t-t_k)/(t_{k+1}-t_k).$$

Strictly increasing finite times and finite samples in $[0,1]$ ensure bounded
linear interpolation over the simulated interval. Excitation is dimensionless;
it is distinct from activation and the resulting force in newtons. Native
muscle activation and compliant-fiber dynamics evolve without state resets.
Configuration and speed retain the model's native coordinate conventions.
No muscle equilibration is applied after restoring supplied initial state.

## Numerical Method and Provenance

One native Manager cold-starts Runge-Kutta-Merson with an explicit accuracy
parameter (default $10^{-8}$) and advances continuously across output times.
The requested time grid is an output/input-knot grid, not the adaptive internal
step sequence. Both reference generation and reproduction must use the same
declared initialization policy. Named continuous states do not serialize
discrete/plugin state or integrator history; broader models remain unsupported
until their initialization is qualified.

The receipt binds model bytes, ordered native state and muscle names, full
continuous initial state, time grid, excitation samples, interpolation,
integrator accuracy, installed provider version and ordered concrete muscle
laws. Adapter `native-muscle-replay/1.3.0` binds the executed subtype policy and
`muscle_class_policy="exact-supported-concrete-law/1.0.0"`. Before native
`initSystem`, recursive admission requires exact concrete identity
`Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle` or `Thelen2003Muscle`. A successful base-class
`safeDownCast` establishes inheritance compatibility only; it cannot qualify an
unknown derived law's state or force semantics. Native casts remain in use for
the supported laws' model-owned state bounds. This guard does not broaden the
existing compliant-tendon, activation, force, constraint or initialization scope.
Native applied excitations
are checked at output times separately from native muscle forces. This local
receipt is a development adapter; the versioned Tools bundle remains the
durable interchange authority. The model file alone is not a complete hash of
arbitrary external resource dependencies, so such models need additional
qualification before use.

## Evidence and Limits

`tests/opensim/test_native_muscle_replay.py` creates a genuine one-DOF native
Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle and Thelen2003Muscle fixtures, including nonzero
activation and compliant fiber state. Tests check independent restored native
force, restoring muscle motion, native applied commands,
same-policy reproduction, tighter-accuracy/output-grid refinement and rejection
of invalid inputs, missing state and hidden drives. This is independent of
capture fitting and is not a physiological parameter validation.

Child #11867 adds a class-identity boundary test that substitutes an unknown
reported class on real native Component/Muscle proxies while retaining
successful native base casts. An initialization trap proves rejection precedes
`initSystem`. This is explicitly proxy boundary evidence, not a loaded or
compiled third-party C++ plugin test. Both unchanged concrete native laws retain
their positive replay tests. New subclasses need their own reviewed state,
force, serialization and initialization policy before admission.

Executed locally with OpenSim 4.6 (2026-06-22-85aaf64), Python 3.12.10:

```powershell
python3 -m pytest tests/opensim/test_native_muscle_replay.py --override-ini='addopts=' -q
```

Use an environment with the reported native provider; optional-provider skips
in other environments do not establish native acceptance. Full-body anatomy,
native contact force traces, grip and club dynamics, reserve audits, uncertainty,
full-horizon mocap accuracy and clean-host reproduction remain required gates.
See the binding [architecture review](../../../docs/development/feedback_controls/ASTRA_REVIEW.md).
